pathways.climate_pressure: April 2014 flooding described in the article's Honiara case.
pathways.documented_impact: People were displaced and faced disaster-related losses.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived inadequacy of government rehabilitation support generated recovery grievances.
pathways.possible_consequence: The article codes a16May 2014 protest-turned-riot; this is one historical case, not a general causal relationship.
alternative_explanations: Disaster-recovery governance and existing political grievances may shape protest independently of the flood. The aggregate study reports a null association.
pathways.uncertainty: Media-coded historical example, not an event-attribution study or quantified mechanism. Do not generalize across settlements, provinces or future disasters.
resilience_factors: Adequate and inclusive recovery assistance is an implied governance consideration, not an evaluated intervention effect.
pathways.compact_statement: One Honiara 2014 case links flood displacement, perceived inadequate rehabilitation and a protest-turned-riot; aggregate study findings do not establish a general disaster-conflict effect.

gaps: The SAGE study's Methods specify 2012-2020, while Discussion mentions13years/936observations. This inconsistency is flagged rather than silently reconciled.
The coordinator could not reopen the government NAP endpoint; its bounded planning claims rely on the collector's original-page extraction.
The World Bank ICR bears a public-disclosure-authorization stamp; no restricted-only document is reproduced.

executive_assessment.text: Named Rendova communities and provincial water investments add local vulnerability and governance detail; project surveys and two-community fieldwork are not representative rankings.

A historical Honiara disaster-recovery grievance case illustrates a possible mechanism, but the same three-country study finds no significant aggregate disaster/temperature association with social conflict.
